title: Production Memory Leak from String Concatenation in Loop
question: Your production application is running out of memory. After profiling, you find a method that processes 10,000 log entries using String concatenation in a loop: for(String log : logs) { result = result + log + '\n'; }. Explain why this causes memory issues, calculate approximate memory usage, and provide the correct solution using StringBuilder. What would be the memory difference?

title: NullPointerException in Production - Root Cause Analysis
question: Your REST API returns 500 errors intermittently with NullPointerException at user.getAddress().getCity(). The stack trace shows it fails only for 10% of requests. Walk through your debugging approach: how do you reproduce it, identify which object is null (user or address), prevent it with null checks, and discuss using Optional<T> as an alternative solution. What logging would you add?

title: File Descriptors Exhausted - Resource Leak Detection
question: Your application crashes after 6 hours with 'Too many open files' error. You suspect file handles aren't being closed. Show three versions of file reading code: (1) bad code without closing, (2) improved with try-finally, (3) best practice with try-with-resources. Explain why try-with-resources is superior and what happens if close() throws an exception. How would you detect this issue before production?

title: HashMap Not Finding Existing Keys - equals/hashCode Bug
question: Users report that your cache keeps creating duplicate User objects even though they have the same userId. Investigation shows HashMap.containsKey() returns false for users that were just added. You discover the User class overrides equals() but not hashCode(). Explain: (1) why this breaks HashMap, (2) the equals-hashCode contract, (3) correct implementation for User class with userId, email, name fields. What happens if you fix hashCode() in production with existing data?

title: String Pool Memory Bloat from User Input
question: Your application accepts millions of unique user messages per day and stores them using: String message = userInput.intern(). After 3 days, the application slows down and memory usage keeps growing despite no memory leaks. Explain: (1) what intern() does, (2) why this causes problems, (3) when String pool memory is freed, (4) the correct approach for storing user-generated content. How would you diagnose this was a String pool issue?
realWorldScenario: Memory issues from incorrect String pool usage

title: Silent Failures - Exception Swallowing Bug
question: Your data import job reports success, but 30% of records are missing from the database. Code review reveals: try { processRecord(record); } catch(Exception e) { logger.error('Error'); }. List all problems with this code: (1) swallowing exceptions, (2) not logging exception details, (3) catching Exception instead of specific types, (4) continuing processing. Provide corrected code with proper exception handling, logging with context, and deciding whether to fail-fast or continue with errors.
realWorldScenario: Debugging silent failures in batch jobs

title: Timezone Bug - Date Stored Incorrectly Across Regions
question: Your global application shows appointments at wrong times for users in different timezones. Investigation reveals you're using LocalDateTime.now() for scheduling and storing it in database without timezone info. When a US user books 2 PM their time, EU users see it at 2 PM their time. Explain: (1) why LocalDateTime is wrong here, (2) difference between LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, and Instant, (3) correct approach using ZonedDateTime or Instant, (4) how to migrate existing data. What timezone should server/database use?
realWorldScenario: Fixing timezone bugs in global applications

title: Deserialization Failure After Class Changes
question: After deploying a new version, your application fails to read previously serialized User objects from disk with InvalidClassException: local class incompatible. You added a new 'phoneNumber' field to User class. Explain: (1) what serialVersionUID is, (2) why it's missing from your class, (3) how to fix this with backward compatibility, (4) strategies for evolving serialized classes (default values, transient fields, custom serialization). How do you recover the old data?

title: Immutable Object Modified - Defensive Copying Bug
question: You created an 'immutable' Config class with final fields including a List<String>. Users report config values change unexpectedly. Code shows: class Config { private final List<String> allowedUsers; public Config(List<String> users) { this.allowedUsers = users; } public List<String> getAllowedUsers() { return allowedUsers; } }. Client code modifies the returned list. Explain: (1) why this breaks immutability, (2) concept of defensive copying, (3) correct implementation for constructor and getter, (4) using Collections.unmodifiableList(). Is final enough for immutability?

title: Method Parameter Confusion - Pass by Value Misconception
question: A junior developer expects this code to modify the price: void updatePrice(Integer price) { price = price + 10; }. When called with updatePrice(productPrice), the productPrice remains unchanged. But modifying a list works: void addItem(List items) { items.add('new'); }. Explain: (1) Java is pass-by-value always, (2) why Integer doesn't change but List does, (3) difference between object reference and object value, (4) how wrapper classes are immutable. Provide examples showing what gets passed to methods.
searchIntent: java pass by value or reference
